title: What If a Tick Bite Made You Allergic to Meat? One Already Does

scenes.text: What if one tick bite made you allergic to meat for years? In America, one already does.
The lone star tick, found from Texas to Maine. Its bite primes your immune system against a sugar called alpha-gal, the same sugar found in beef, pork and lamb.
Your immune system learns to attack the sugar. Weeks later you eat a burger. Nothing happens. For two to six hours.
Then hives, vomiting, a swelling throat, blood pressure crashing. Life-threatening anaphylaxis, hours after dinner.
Gelatin, milk, even some medicines can trigger it. In a survey of 1,500 clinicians, nearly half had never heard of the condition.
The CDC counted over 110,000 suspected cases since 2010 and estimates up to 450,000 Americans have it. Cases are now turning up in states where the tick isn't even supposed to live.

description:
What if a tick bite could make you allergic to meat? Alpha-gal syndrome does exactly that: the lone star tick's bite sensitizes people to a sugar molecule found in mammal meat, so beef, pork, lamb, gelatin and even some dairy and medicines can trigger reactions that start 2 to 6 hours after eating, from hives to life-threatening anaphylaxis.
The CDC identified more than 110,000 suspected cases between 2010 and 2022 and estimates up to 450,000 people in the US may be affected; in a survey of 1,500 clinicians, nearly half had never heard of it. Most cases are in southern and eastern states where the tick lives, with clusters appearing further north.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Between 2017 and 2022 more than 300,000 blood samples were tested for alpha-gal antibodies and over 30 percent came back positive. Which animal would you least like to be bitten by? Drop your own what-if below.
